---
id: cpp-sw-at-most-k-changes
title: Longest Run with at Most k Changes
difficulty: Medium
order: 7
tags: sliding window, strings, greedy
time_limit: 1
---
## Statement
Two "budget of k changes" windows:

```cpp
int max_ones_with_flips(const std::vector<int>& bits, int k);
    // longest run of 1s after flipping at most k zeros to 1
int longest_after_replacements(const std::string& s, int k);
    // longest substring of ONE repeated letter after replacing at most k characters (uppercase A–Z)
```

- **Flips:** the window `[L, R]` is valid while it contains at most `k` zeros.
- **Replacements:** the window is valid while `length − (count of its most frequent letter) ≤ k`. Those are the characters you would replace.

`"AABABBA"` with k = 1 gives 4: replace the `B` in `"AABA"` to get `"AAAA"`. `[1,1,0,0,1,1,1,0,1]` with k = 1 gives 5.

**Input:** cases until the end of input: `flips n k` + n bits, or `replace k s`. n ≤ 10⁶.

## Starter
```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

int max_ones_with_flips(const vector<int>& bits, int k) {
    int best = 0, run = 0;
    for (int b : bits) { run = b ? run + 1 : 0; best = max(best, run); }   // ignores k
    return best;
}
int longest_after_replacements(const string& s, int k) { return 0; }
```

## Driver
```cpp
int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr);
    string cmd;
    while (cin >> cmd) {
        if (cmd == "flips") {
            int n, k; cin >> n >> k;
            vector<int> b(n); for (auto& x : b) cin >> x;
            cout << max_ones_with_flips(b, k) << '\n';
        } else {
            int k; string s; cin >> k >> s;
            cout << longest_after_replacements(s, k) << '\n';
        }
    }
}
```

## Hints
- For flips, the window is valid while it holds at most k zeros. Shrink when it holds more.
- For replacements, the number of changes a window needs is `length − (count of its most common letter)`.
- You don't need to decrease the "max frequency" when shrinking: an outdated larger value never produces a wrong maximum length.

## Solution
**Flips.** Count the zeros in the window. More than `k` means the window can't become all ones, so shrink. The longest valid window is the answer.

**Replacements.** To turn a window into one repeated letter, keep its most frequent letter and replace the rest: `len − maxFreq` changes. Valid means `len − maxFreq ≤ k`.

The subtle trick: `maxf` is **never decreased** when the window shrinks, so it may be stale (larger than the true current maximum). That's still correct for finding the *maximum length*. A stale `maxf` can only keep the window *longer* than strictly valid, but it never lets `best` exceed a length that was truly achieved: `best` grows only when `maxf` itself grows, at a moment when that frequency was real. It also saves recomputing the maximum over 26 counts.

Complexity: O(n) each.

```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

int max_ones_with_flips(const vector<int>& bits, int k) {
    int L = 0, zeros = 0, best = 0;
    for (int R = 0; R < (int)bits.size(); ++R) {
        zeros += bits[R] == 0;
        while (zeros > k) zeros -= bits[L++] == 0;
        best = max(best, R - L + 1);
    }
    return best;
}

int longest_after_replacements(const string& s, int k) {
    array<int, 26> cnt{};
    int L = 0, maxf = 0, best = 0;
    for (int R = 0; R < (int)s.size(); ++R) {
        maxf = max(maxf, ++cnt[s[R] - 'A']);            // most frequent letter seen in any window so far
        while (R - L + 1 - maxf > k) --cnt[s[L++] - 'A'];
        best = max(best, R - L + 1);
    }
    return best;
}
```
